Flat out, this is THE definitive version of Dark Souls 2 to own. This is the version you buy if you're interested in this game. All 3 DLC's, plus an added boss with Scholar of the First Sin. Improved graphics. Improved multiplayer. 6 person co-op. Added items. Better enemy placement. This version has it all.
However, some people feel that this edition is a "cash grab", when that simply isn't true. Look at what you're getting. For a measly $30(if you already own DkS2) you get: improved game engine, improved graphics, improved multiplayer, harder enemies, increased co-op online cap, ALL THREE DLC'S WHICH COST AS MUCH AS THIS GAME DOES ON IT'S OWN, and then you're also supporting the developers of one of the best game series of recent times. If that's not a bargain, well, show me one then. Even for the full price of $50, read that list a couple of sentences ago and tell me it's still not a bargain. People dump THOUSANDS of hours into this game, $50 for nearly unlimited replayability is a bargain if I've ever seen one.
I'm also seeing alot of people complain that this game doesn't work for them. "I can't get past the menu" "My character is distorted" "my mouse is buggy". Guaranteed that most of these people did not check and verify that they were buying the correct version, DX9 vs DX11. PROTIP: It's not the developers problem to make sure you buy the right game. If they made this game for OSX, and you bought the OSX version instead of the Windows versions, it's no ones fault but your own. It is entirely the end users responsibility to make sure their PC can handle the software being run on it. No one gives Ford crap for the Fiesta being slow, because they know what they're getting into. Don't give Bamco crap for your PC not running the game when 9 chances out of 10, your PC can't support it anyway. I will get alot of flak for this because Steam users are notoriously up in themselves about their PC knowledge, and are infallible in their IT skills, but, alas, they're probably doing it wrong. If you can't get this game to run, you're doing it wrong, and that's all there is to it.
Speaking on PC requirements, for a DX11 game, these are incredibly low. I'm actually surprised at how low these requirements are, which just speaks to the above paragraph about how people are just doing it wrong. I first tested this game running on a 2011-era laptop with a Quadro GPU(you know, the ones that "aren't for gaming") on good ol' Windows 8(you know, the OS that "doesn't work"), and man, it ran super smooth and crystal clear. No stutter, no issues, all high details, 60FPS all day long. Once again, if you can't get this game to run, you're doing it wrong.
So yeah. I highly recommend this game for anyone interested in Dark Souls 2, or is looking to get the DLC finally, or really even for people who already have the DLC, have beaten it several times and are just looking for something new. Ignore the haters, they don't know what they're talking about :)

I bought this game during this year's summer sale to experiment with my friends, and it ended up becoming my favorite shooter by far, even beating out long-time runners BF3 and CoD: MW. There's just something to be said about the harsh struggles of the First World War, with almost every weapon capable of killing in just a single bullet.
The weapons are almost perfectly balanced, with perhaps the exception of the infamously mediocre Chauchat (I personally enjoy using it, though maybe not as much as the Lewis), and the asymmetrical maps offer each side an equal number of yet different vantage points and killboxes. In addition, the models are very accurate, though as Ian of ForgottenWeapons, who plays this game, will tell you, the French rifles have a slight error in their sight pictures.
This game is a high-risk, high-reward team-based game. The individual can accomplish much, but without any communication many games devolve into giant stalemates, alternating between attacking and defending. That being said, even a single squad communicating within itself is enough to turn the tide, and if one manages to get the entire team on voice chat they would be nigh unstoppable. Even a single machine gunner with enough cues from his comrades is enough to suppress the entire enemy team, forestalling their advance until the next phase.
Of course, every game has its downsides. For all its gameplay features, joining games with your friends is a little bit of a hassle. On the lower-populated AU server, it is nigh impossible to get your private squad into a game, instead having to rely on joining an already-existing squad and hoping no randoms join. The visuals are not something you would consider modern, and combined with some choppy animations sometimes the game looks clunky.
On the whole, though, Verdun is a fresh breath into a market saturated with head-turning, three-dimensional twitch shooters and gritty military simulators, introducing both a unique setting and simple yet appropriate mechanics. I heartily recommend this game.

Types of white wines:
Chardonnay, gewürztraminer, moscato are white grape varieties. This page describes wine styles by variety and production area. Any below variety can give dry white wine or sweet white wine. Some varieties can be made bubbly or still.
If only one variety (chardonnay, gewürztraminer) is mentioned on the label, then the wine is called varietal and is named after the grape with a capital initial (Chardonnay, Gewürztraminer). Varietal wines primarily show the fruit: how the wines tastes much depends on the grape variety.

Chardonnay
Picture of chardonnay vine
Chardonnay vine
(Shar-do-nay) Chardonnay was the most popular white grape through the 1990's. It can be made sparkling or still.
Food pairings: a good choice for fish (even salmon) and chicken dishes.
Districts: chardonnay makes the principle white wine of Burgundy (Bourgogne, France), where it originated. Chardonnay is versatile and is grown with success in most viticultural areas under a variety of climatic conditions. Yet it only amounts to 2 percent of the world vine areas. Total chardonnay vines cover more than 160,000 hectares (400,000 acres). The biggest states were in 2005:
U.S.A.: California: 44,509 ha; Oregon and Washington state: 3,200 ha
France: 35,252 ha
Australia: 22,528 ha
Italy: 11,800 ha
Moldavia: 6,000 ha
South Africa: 8,000 ha
Chili: 7,500 ha
Argentina: 5,155 ha
Typical taste of the different types of chardonnay: voluptuous. Chardonnay wines are often wider-bodied (and more velvety) than other types of dry whites, with rich citrus (lemon, grapefruit) flavors. Fermenting in new oak barrels adds a buttery tone (vanilla, toast, coconut, toffee). Tasting a USD 20 Californian Chardonnay should give citrus fruit flavors, hints of melon, vanilla, some toasty character and some creaminess. Burgundy whites can taste very different.

Sauvignon blanc
Sauvignon blanc
Sauvignon blanc
(So-veen-yawn Blah)
Food pairings: a versatile food wine for seafood, poultry, and salads.
Districts: of French origin, sauvignon blanc is grown in the Bordeaux region where it is blended with semillon. The Loire valley and New Zealand produce some excellent sauvignon blanc varietals. Some Australian Sauvignon Blancs, grown in warmer areas, tends to be flat and lack fruit qualities.
Typical taste in varietal wine: sauvignon blanc normally shows a herbal character suggesting bell pepper or freshly mown grass. The dominating flavors range from sour green fruits of apples, pears and gooseberries through to tropical fruits of melon, mango and blackcurrant. Quality unoaked Sauvignon Blancs will display smokey qualities; they require bright aromas and a strong acid finish and are best grown in cool climates.

Semillon
(Say-mee-yaw)
Food pairings: Semillon goes with fish but there are many better matches. Serve dry Semillon with clams, mussels, or pasta salad.
Districts: sémillon is the major white grape in the Bordeaux region of France. Sémillon is also known as Hunter (River Riesling), boal/bual of Madeira, chevrier, columbier, malaga and blanc doux. Sémillon is also grown in Chile, Argentina, Australia, and California.
Typical taste: the wine varietal features distinct fig-like character. Sémillon is often blended with sauvignon blanc to delimit its strong berry-like flavors.
From the Bordeaux region of France come the great Sauternes and Barsac. These wines are produced from overripe sémillon grapes. They are blended with sauvignon blanc to produce a syrupy, full-bodied wine that may be world class.

Moscato
Muscat vine picture
Muscat vine picture
(Mos-cato) The moscato variety belongs to the muscat family of grapes - and so do moscatel and muscat ottonel.
Food pairings: Moscato shows best on its own: without food but sweet wines will pair with dessert.
Districts: moscato grows in most vine-friendly climates, including Italy, the Rhône Valley (where it is called muscat blanc à petits grains) and Austria (where it is called Muskateller).
Typical taste: often sweet and always fruity, with a characteristic grapefruity and musky aroma. Moscato wines are easily recognizable to anyone who has tasted a Muscat table grape.

Pinot grigio
Picture of pinot gris
Picture of pinot gris
(Pee-no gree-zo)
Food pairings: versatile.
Districts: pinot grigio is planted extensively in the Venezia and Alto Adige regions of Italy. Pinot grigio is also grown in the western coastal regions of the U.S.A. It is called malvoisie in the Loire Valley and pinot gris in the rest of France. In Germany and Austria pinot grigio is known as the Ruländer or Grauer Burgunder. Similar aliases are used in the german settled regions of Australia.
Typical taste: crisp, dry wines with good acid "bite" are typically made in Italy and Germany. Oregon or Alsace Pinot Gris shows aromatic, fruity flavors. Pairing with food is more difficult because Alsatian winemakers leave the grapes on the vine much longer. The perfume in Alsatian Pinot Gris makes it especially well suited for Thai or spicy Chinese cuisine.

Gewürztraminer
Gewürztraminer vine picture
Gewürztraminer
(Gah-vurtz-tra-meener) A very aromatic variety.
Food pairings: gewürztraminer is ideal for sipping. It can fit Asian food, pork and grilled sausages.
Districts: gewürztraminer is best known in wines from Alsace, Germany, the U.S. West Coast, and New York.
Typical taste in varietal wine: fruity flavors with aromas of rose petals, peaches, lychees, and allspice. A Gewürztraminer seems generally not as refreshing as other types of dry whites.

Riesling
Old Vine of riesling
Old Vine of riesling
(Rees-ling)
Food pairings: dry versions go well with fish, chicken and pork dishes. The crispiness of a Riesling works very well with tuna and salmon while the acidity level intermingles with the slight smokiness of the eel and cuts through the layers of spicier Japanese foods.
Districts: the classic German grape of the Rhine and Mosel, riesling grows in all wine regions. Germany's great Rieslings are usually made slightly sweet, with steely acidity for balance. Riesling from Alsace and the Eastern U.S. is also excellent, though usually made in a different style, equally aromatic but typically drier (not sweet). California Rieslings are much less successful, usually sweet without sufficient acidity for balance.
Typical taste in varietal wine: Riesling wines are much lighter than Chardonnay wines. The aromas generally include fresh apples. The riesling variety expresses itself very differently depending on the district and the winemaking. Rieslings should taste fresh. If they do, then they might also prove tastier and tastier as they age.

Review:
This game's pace is deceiving, it goes from quiet, nail biting stalemates eyes peeled on a trench some odd hundred meters away, to charging into narrow confined trenches with a bolt action weapon. So be prepared for a change of pace from usual shooters. The one hit kill with the bolt action makes this game even more difficult, but makes the squad roles even more valuable as grenades, supressing MGs and artillery are invaluable for breaking a line of rifle men. It essentially forces a cohesion in pub and competative matches alike that is unseen in many other squad/role based FPS games. Heavily reminds me of red orchestra which is a great thing as far as im concerned. The crouching, and prone can feel "clunky" at times, and finding the right angle to perch an MG is always a pain, but overall the game is very playable in its beta state and the promise of new content keeps it interesting. Maps are immersive and hard to navigate, but once you get routes down they become less intimidating, The desertion mechanic keeps the battlefields in a consolidated enough condition to avoid players running around in a massive map unable to find foes *cough cough battlefield*, and it makes flanking hard....very hard. Which makes the positions that are flankable centers of close combat. This shifts the pace from intense close quarters brawling to long sniper-counter-sniper wars in no-mans land.
Overall Verdun is an excellant game, the gameplay mechanics are simple yet effective to make a smooth FPS.

The design chances pertaining to enemy and item/key placement are a major gamechanger, things make more sense now both thematically and design-wise. Things like ledges and vertical space are better used in the form of sniper enemies and mages you can take out to make an encounter easier beforehand, enemy types are also utilized better, better use of level design like that enhances the game and makes it feel like Miyazaki Souls, even though it isn't.
The world space is the same, but this remake utilizes it MUCH better. Veterans of the original one I think will be amazed at how the changes affect the game for the better, and how easier it is to make varied builds with important items being accessible earlier (Dull Ember comes to mind, as well as some weapons like the Greatsword).
The way they integrate DLC into the world also makes it feel like it was always there from the start, not addons, which is great.
The lighting is much better and more natural looking now, the strong orange glow is gone from daytime areas replaced with a more natural looking sunlight look, and dark areas have more contrast to them (the torch is needed in some areas if it's your first time exploring it, too bad we veterans already know their layout so we don't get this benefit).
There are also multiplayer improvements, with 6 player active multiplayer and "pools of blood" packing multiple bloodstain deaths into one (very amusing if you check the ones near pits).
Overall, this is the DS2 that should have been in the first place. Are you willing to put the upgrade asking price to experience what you should have gotten in the first place? You decide, but if you're a newcomer then don't even think about getting the old version, get this one.
And if you own the old version but not the Season Pass, it's also a no-brainer since it's only $5 more than the DLC on its own.
Great redesign of the game, I'm certain this version will be the one leaving its legacy over the years, as this is what DS2 should have been considering its circumstances.

tl;dr: A definite must have if you're into online fps games. Endless user content and playtime overshadows breaks from modern fps mechanics and graphics.
What it does right: Valve definitely knew what they were doing when they made this game. The base game is tons of fun on its own, including ways to make your own matches with bots if you don't have an internet connection. The Terrorist/Counterterrorist thing is a welcome visual change from the typical American/Russian/Middle Eastern warfare we're so used to with shooters. You get pretty much was it says on the tin at first--no story, no unlock progression, no fancy customization system--just a multiplayer fps with a handfull of different maps and either a bomb plant/diffusal or hostage rescue type of game. Don't get me wrong, these on their own are great fun, especially with a group of friends, but that's not where this game really shines.
There are so many possibilities when it comes to game type with this game. From Zombie, adventure, surfing, and gun game mods, there is a ton of hours to be had searching through servers to try out new things. With the support to create and play on your own maps too, there's an absolutely massive amount of content to try out. Take a look on fpsbanana, or whatever they're calling themselves these days and you'll know what I mean. You can even change the textures of your weapons and the enemies and friendlies to your specific tastes with the magnitude of skins there are out there for grabs.
Trust me when I say that if you're going to try out something, do gungame. It's an absolute cluster♥♥♥♥ on smaller maps, and it's amazing. There's a reason big budget fps games decided to add their own variant of it. Also, surf maps are a little hard to get used to, but they're is a lot of fun to be had once you get the hang of it. A lot of these maps you can even enjoy without firing a single shot.
What it does wrong: I'll admit, it took me a minute to actually think up any flaws for this game, so they aren't that big of a deal.
The game is almost ten years old by now, and with the age, some things may seem hard to get used to for mainstream fps players that started only recently. For starters, there's no iron sights in this game. I can hear the shocked gasps already, but it really isn't that big of a hinderance. The guns all work well enough without them, even if it would be preferrable if we could zoom in on our targets with every gun like we're used to. Another outdated feature is having to earn money in-match for all the guns you want to play with. This means the first round is always a pistol round in traditional maps, and if you don't do particularly well, you might end up stuck with it for a while. Also having to go through the menu and purchase your loadout every time you die. You'll get familiar with the hotkeys very quickly if you don't want to get left behind before the round starts.
Another thing in the base game that's a bit outdated is the inclusion of respawning only at the beginning of a new match. Being used to just jumping in after a few seconds is something you're going to have to grow out of unless you want to stick to something like gungame.
Lastly, it's definitely not as pretty as the triple A titles out today, so if you're one of those types that prefers graphics over actual gameplay, look elsewhere.
Overall, it's a great game and a must-have for any hardcore online fps player. Being one of valves top games, a good chunk of steam users are going to have it, so you're not going to run out of people to play with. Endless content for it mean constantly discovering new ways to play with the same old tools. If you can get over some outdated features and less-than-ideal graphics, then you definitely need to pick up this game.

Overall the concept of this game is great.  Authentic weapons, map, scenery, squad based play are top notch.  But it definitely needs some polishing.  My biggest gripe is the lag and choppy play.  If your ping rate is low I'm sure all the much better.  I hover around 100 for the most part.  There are times I know I get the drop on an enemy yet he manages to shoot me first.   This typically happens with enemy players whose ping rates are half of mine.  This gets quite frustrating after a while.  Also I experienced a weird anamoly where I start falling thru the ground and air continuously in certain sections of certain maps.  The only way to get out of it is to change characters in the squad menu and re-spawn.  The barb wire, although it is a nice authentic feature in the game, can also be a pain dealing with.  Yeah I understand it's something you get tangled up in but I should be able to back out of it the way I came in.  Instead I just end up bunny hopping around until I either succumb to it or the enemy shoots me.  Other than that this is a really good game.  I hope to continue playing but I would like to see some serious fixes to the game play to keep me interested in it over the long run.  Also, how about some mechanized attacks?  Tanks would be nice.  Perhaps a leading squad could earn one during game play as a bonus.

A gaming style very similar to GTA, with a slight twist. You are actually trying to make the world a better place and you have a cool grappling hook and parachute to help you do it. Oh, and a ton of adrenaline filled action to go along with it. Similar to GTA, you can hijack vehicles,♥♥♥♥♥♥off the authorities(Heat), complete story missions and side quests. Just Cause takes it a little further to give you a moral reason to fight.
There are a few downsides that arent too drastic. Sometimes travelling may seem to take forever and the landscape can get a little repetitive. As you play though, you will realise that its just a matter of finding the right transport. Also, a key aspect of the game is 'Chaos' which is generated when you destroy government marked utilities, complete missions and destroy millitary establishments. So instead of just going from mission A to mission B, you have something to keep you busy while you travel.
A must buy for anyone liking the GTA genre.

The graphics take an obvious resemblance to Crysis (no duh, it's developed in CryEngine), and the gameplay reminds of a slower but more awkward Rainbow Six. So, by all means, give this game a try! It's perfectly functional, but it probably won't keep your attention for long.

[Minor Spoiler] The early vendor selling the Fragrant Branch of Yore gives you MUCH more freedom to choose your own path in this one. I'm enjoying that muchly.
I'm a bit disappointed in FROM Software though. They have been well aware of the 60fps durability bug and yet have not addressed it in this release. For those unaware, the game engine calculates certain things like jump distance, invulnerability key frames, and how much durability a weapon loses per swing based on the assumption of a 30fps game. FROM set the FPS to 60 for the PC and because these calculations were not adjusted it means you jump shorter distances, have fewer invulnerability frames, and lose weapon durability TWICE AS FAST. Its incredibly brutal, and can result in you losing up to 6 points of weapon durability for hitting a corpse! I had applied a patch called DS2Fix from a modder called eur0pa on the original DS2 and the return of this bug is especially painful. Since most of the areas seem balanced around the expected weapon degradation you basically need to carry 2 weapons, or 2 copies of the same weapon, to clear areas.
Anyway. I would wait to buy this until eur0pa fixes it. I'm going to be playing but I keep butting heads with that durability issue.. and repair powder is so expensive!

This is like TF2 in World War II.

If you are reading this you're likely between the rich ages of 18 and 32, and have a mere 25 years before being nearly legally required to watch World War II documentaries on the History Channel every weekend, grunting at your friends and making increasingly ridiculous what-if scenarios involving George Patton, Anton Dostler, and the occult. So why play another game in the oversaturated WWII market? Or worse, a modern warfare game, probably involving Tom Clancy, the Jim Davis of war media.
Instead, experience the most brutal war in history in hideous detail. Our greatest historians can barely parse how this crime against God happened, and Verdun delivers upon its promise to bring you into a tortured hell of screaming peasants. This game has it all: gas, mud, lonely and pointless death, shovels, biplanes, and more. And just when you thought you had it figured out, what seems to be an 8 foot tall German with eyes as black as coal leaps into a trench and impales a squadron of blase Frenchmen on his pickelhaub before killing himself with his own grenade. If you can't appreciate that, then I feel sorry for you.
I honestly can't think of a work of art that better captures its subject matter than Verdun. You will die in a pit of metaphorical sorrow and literal feces many times. But likely you're picking up that this is not a game for the faint of heart. If you can keep your resolve it will all be worth it when you strike at the heart of the enemy and take from him (or her) the fetid hole of sweat and misery that they never really wanted in the first place. However, don't feel too good about yourself yet, because likely your pig-headed, Zapp Brannigan-esque squad captain will direct you into another suicide mission with all the tactical know-how of your average steer. Just like the real World War I!
I haven't mentioned the graphics or sound or whatever because it doesn't matter. They're good, and irrelevant. The strength of the game though is in the artistry of embodying the war, and provides a rich, satisfying, emotional experience; not unlike a bottle of whisky, black coffee, or reading this review. If you're not convinced of the game's merits yet, there's nothing I can do to help you. Though come to think of it, if you are convinced, I can't help you either because I'm likely getting detached retinas from my position getting shelled for the eigth time this round. I just hope this League of Nations thing works out.

At the time of writing this review, the amount of negative reviews were outnumbering positive ones. This review represented my thoughts about the game as well as the negetive response to the game. Now that the game has mostly positive reviews, I feel  vindicated for taking a more level headed view at the game at the time.
Dark Souls 2 Scholar of the First Sin, has been described as a cash grab, just a patch, and overpriced by some members of the steam community. At this point I am about 9 hours in, and have decided to check in, to describe my experiance to those still on the fence. I own DS2 with all DLC, the value proposition of this remastered edition is a difficult question, which I am not qualified to answer for you personally. Rest assured though if you are a Dark Souls fan you will not be dissapointed, if you "upgrade."
This game feels like finding a great remix to a song you already love. It finds new and interesting ways to surprise you. I have spent 200 Hours in DS2 DX9, and this game has completely refreshed the the experiance for me. That initial feeling of discovery suspense and dread is back! The first few weeks after a souls game comes out, when things are not written in stone and theres still so much to learn and find, thats what make these games great.
There are little touches throughout the game where its like the developers acknowledged every memorable moment and situation and asked "how can we make this more ♥♥♥♥ed up?" Its absolutely diabolical how these "tip of the hat" moments perfectly counter your accepted truths about the game. You spent all of DS2 conditioning yourself to every situation, I think you will find that this game uses everything you have learned  against you.
The solo experiance is even more difficult now, although this can be mitigated by summoning more friends to aid you. In fact right now, with a excess of summon signs it may make the experiance too easy for experianced Souls players. It is nice to have the option if you find yourself in a frustrating situation or for a speed run.
Graphically, the game looks great, although I dont see any major diffences from the DX9 version. Armor and weapons look slightly clearer, but don't expect new HD textures or anything like that. Ive always been happy with the way the game looked, initial gameplay trailers be damned. Performance wise it seems to be running even better then the DX9 version. I use a 660m GTX card on a two year old laptop, everything set to high and it plays pretty smooth.
If you are a Dark Souls fan looking for an excuse to get back into it, I'd say go for it! For me the $20 for Dark Souls 2 remix edition is fine, although I understand that some people may hold remasters to a higher standard and expect more bang for thier buck. All I can say is I took the risk and I am fully enjoying the experiance again. This may split the multiplayer community, and I can see this as problem in the future. Although, Currently it feels like the MP community has simply been refreshed. It feels like the first week of the DX9 release with summon signs everywhere! Scholar of the First Sin maybe a cash grab, just a patch and overpriced, but I dont care... It's more Dark Souls damn it, Praise the Sun!

The story is what really makes this game so good, Its a mature, compelling narrative primarily told through audio-diaries and random pieces of literature you pick up.
Its not a very long game though, with my playthrough clocking in at around 75 minutes. Although you probably don't believe me about the lack of monsters or scares, once you finish the game and discover this for yourself, It is interesting to replay the game without that forboding atmosphere.
Despite the short length and lack of "game like" elements, I would absolutely recommend this game.
Gameplay: Literally all you do is walk around a big house, read things and listen to stuff.
Graphics: Its running in one of my favorite engines, Unity. It looks great, though I would recommend having a fairly decent computer to run it on.
Story: Fantastic, though I can't say much more about it without ruining the game.
Overall: 10/10

Minor Spoilers...With 600 hours put into the original Dark Souls 2 release and now with 10 hours (1/5 to 1/4 of the first playthrough) into Scholar of the First Sin, I can say the changes are immediate and vast. Most people are only aware of the graphical enhancements and 6 player online changes to this version. Let me state that's not why I bought this version at all. I'll still get it out of the way though. The graphics are great now. They colors are now vivid, the textures higher res, and the lighting is phenomenal. I honestly haven't done a lot of co op or pvp yet so I'll skip that one.
The reason I bought it was for the gameplay changes. A majority of the enemies are in different places. Also nearly every encounter has more enemies/different enemies to fit better with the pacing, lore, and challenge. The item placement is also different. It's not game changing but it definitely changes how you might plan out your characters' first run. The enemy AI is great now (these changes have a big impact on the game believe it or not). NPC invaders play a lot like real people. Normal enemies also have higher aggro distances, are more aggresive, and pursue you through the entire map as well. There are also more 'roaming' enemies that surely change up how you tackle certain areas. There's a wide variety of new NPC summons and invaders that have unique playstyles.
Lighting in this isn't just about the graphics either. It changes gameplay by making great use of the torch mechanics that weren't really explored in the first release. There's an emphasis on exploration with new statues to 'unfreeze' and explore the areas they block off, a mechanic that was barely used before as well. A unique and interesting tug of war oriented fps set in WWI. This game is not an a fully accurate simulation, preferring to instead focus on arcade-y squad based tactical shooter  game play centered around pushing the momentum of an attack on an enemy trench or desperately defending your own trench against an onslaught of Allied (or Central) forces. Each side will take turns attacking each others trenches. If one side does well in the attack (by occupying the enemy trench, therefore gaining a "foothold"), your teams attack builds "momentum" and you are granted more time to attack and eventually capture the enemy trench. A battlefield is usually made up of 5 trenches representing about a mile or so of territory between them.
The game is both exhilarating and frustrating. There is a rush of excitement and fear as you leap over the side of your trench to charge across no-man's-land and explosions burst in your eardrums and bullets from Machine Gun emplacements whiz past your head, but that excitement can be ended by the frustration of being shot from a mile away by an enemy you can't see which will happen most of the time if your not careful.
The most interesting part of the game to me is it's setting. As far as I know, this is the only shooter set in WWI and it's depicted in incredible detail. The game may not be an accurate presentation of WWI as far as game mechanics go (such as bullet drop and squad spawn) but the weapons of the war, the sounds of the war, and the depictions of gruesome, destroyed battlefields are amazing. Besides that, the game is very fun which is something I wouldn't have expected from a game about a war where people largely sat in wet trenches for months at a time before getting randomly shot or dying of the  flu.
Fans of multiplayer FPS's and WWI history buffs should give this game a try. There is nothing else like it out there right now.

This wasn't so much a game as it was an interactive story. In fact, as the description says, it's a puzzle that you piece together at your own pace. It's still a very strange game with a spooky atmosphere.
It's interesting that the game feels like a survival horror, yet there's nothing otherworldly to fear. You really can play at your own pace - but it recreates what it would be like to be in a large house, at night, in a storm - it's the addition of being alone, and having no immediate explanation as to where everyone is that creates suspense. It definitely drops little elements of horror in the game, and leaves your mind to fill in the blanks - all while getting a bit creeped out by the thunder outside or the creaking noises the house emits.
I think the ending will leave people feeling a bit disappointed, or expecting a twist. The twist is that there is no twist. I was pleasantly surprised and had a chuckle at myself for succumbing to the tense atmosphere. I love that the game is set in the early-to-mid '90s as it gives it a bit more character. It feature some Riot Grrrl bands which are a fun addition - especially because '90s Alternative Rock and Grunge are mainstay genres on my playlist.
The story was slow paced. It was quite nice to see/hear it unfold. If it was told in a different format (such as a film) it might not work, or feel padded out. Adding the story in to a mystery/exploration certainly worked, however.
A few gripes I have are the price and the graphics. The price should be about a third of what they're asking for (£14.99 as of 09/06/14), in my opinion. It's a short game - taking me about 4 hours to complete, and I don't think that justifies the asking price. Combined with the graphics, which aren't spectacular - yet they still manage to slow my system down even on the lowest settings. The game was still immersive without high end graphics, again, I just wish they weren't so intense for my system to handle... it's not like I was running Crysis 3!
With all the extra content this game could easily eat up 100+ hours of your time. So grab a couple two liters of your choice cola and prepare for hours of fun.

(6 hours played, retrospective)
Your character has to explore an unfamiliar mansion at night, during a thunderstorm, to uncover clues to the whereabouts of your missing family. On the surface, this sounds like a horror/thriller adventure, which is why I can see why many people are turned off by this game. However, I'm a fan of unexpected genre shifts when done right; like the way Alfred Hitchcock subverted Psycho from an embezzlement crime drama to a slasher film.
The similarities can be drawn further by recognizing the voyeuristic undertones of searching the house top to bottom for clues. You'll be raiding your parents' and sibling's personal effects to piece together their lives, as well as their wherabouts. Despite the moody atmosphere, you'll realize by the end that

. The ominous undertones still serves the purpose of creating a layer of tension, which helps motivate the player forward. I can't imagine the game being as compelling on the first playthrough without it.
With "playing" in mind, I wouldn't consider this a game as much as an exploratory narrative in the same vein as Dear Esther - another polarizing, but critically acclaimed interactive story in it's own right. The more rewarding aspects of this game is finding objects that trigger a voiceover from the player's younger sister. Her voice is the only one you hear throughout the entire game, and her journey in establishing her identity during the tribulations of high school is captured beautifully.
Another thing I'd like to point out is the time period. It's set in 1995, since cell phones would mitigate this game, altogether. It also important to factor this in when you discover a central theme to the story. You'll know it when you see it. The importance didn't dawn on me until months after playing the game. This also probably means they were targeting a specific demographic of gamers in their 30's. I spent my formative years in the 90's, so this game gives me a fresh perspective on things I didn't have the maturity to realize back then.
All in all, I think this isn't a game for everyone, especially younger gamers. Otherwise, you'll have to play it yourself. Personally, I found it very engrossing.

2013 was a strong year for games that furthered storytelling in gaming, with both «The last of us» and «Beyond: Two Souls» that lifted the medium to a new level. Still a game by a tiny gaming company consisting of four people beats them both, and that game is «Gone Home».
You're a young woman that arrives home to the US after a trip around Europe. It's the night to the 7th of june 1995 and you arrive to an empty house. Neither your younger sister or your parents are home, but you still get into the house. To figure out what has happend you have to explore the house. Through letters, notes, diaries etc. you piece together a story about a family and a teenage girl that's growing up.
The story feels very personal, painful, warm and beautiful. The game managed something no games have managed before, which is to bring tears to my eyes. It's fairly short, 2-3 hours, but in that timespan it engaged me more than most games can manage in 10-20 hours.
If you have even the tinies interest for gaming this is a game you have to play. Buy it, find three hours to sit down alone and play it. You won't regret it.

So far I've yet to find myself impressed with this update. A few smatterings of pretty lighting, some fancy particle effects, and (extra) enemies placed in new places, which allow them cheap shots on veterans and new players alike. It feels like I paid $30 (Upgrade + DLC) for a version of Dark Souls II that was edited by a bored teenager, giggling as he sticks enemies all over the place and randomly puts graphical sliders on maximum. Every "bone" the original game would throw you is now gone. In their place, a hollow waits to stagger you as three of his friends stunlock you to death. I'd rather go back to playing Bloodborne. By comparison Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin feels clunky, awkward, and artificially difficult. It's hard to believe this was brought to us by the same company that created Demon's Souls, Dark Souls, and Bloodborne. This wasn't worth starting a new game for, much less paying money. Modders have already outdone this 'update' in less time, for free, and with better support. I'm disappointed with you, From Software.
::EDIT::
To be fair, I have noticed this game runs better on my PC as opposed to its predecessor. I had to fiddle with graphics settings in the DX9 version, and I can have everything set to High + Resolution Oversampling and still get completely smooth performance. The combat, however, still feels slow and sluggish, especially compared to the original Dark Souls title and the new Bloodborne. 60 FPS means nothing if your character handles like he's mud wrestling. Speaking of 60 FPS, weapon degredation is positively awful as it's based on frame rate (intended for the ~30 FPS of a console) so your weapons can break in minutes on this port.

I played Dark Souls 2 for almost 1000 hours and had a blast. So when Scholar of the first Sin was announced, I had no doubt in my mind that I will get it.
And it is awesome. In a way, I feel like this is the version Dark Souls 2 should have always had been. The changes are in the details, but they matter. The look is much more crisp, dark areas are really dark, bright ones really bright, etc. The enemy placements now make sense and the mobs you fight are much more varied. Item placement is also improved, giving you helpful stuff earlier, but some other things you have to look out for later.
The game has definitely become harder, but in a good way. There are many new encounters which will have you clench your buttocks, but this is how Souls games should be.
All in all, Scholar of the first Sin manages to feel like a new game as well as feel immediately familiar.
No matter if you upgrade or if you come in as a new player, this is the definitive version of  Dark Souls 2, and it is worth every cent.

Original review:
I would not recommend this to players new to the Souls series, or even to those who haven't yet bought the DLC for the original DS2.
As it is now, the game is not challenging, it's just unfair.
Dark Souls 2 arguably wasn't as good a game as Dark Souls 1, but it was still a great game.
Scholar of the First Sin is a bad refresh of that great game.
Graphics aside, the new enemy placements are horrendous, especially in the starting zones. While FROM were keen to show how many enemies they can put in the area, they didn't rebalance the strength of those enemies, or the durability of your weapons.
It's now not uncommon to face 15+ enemies in a single area, with your weapon breaking from durability loss in the process.
Strong enemies are in places they shouldn't be, and others just in areas that make no sense.
The Heide Knights used to be a test of strength and skill, but now they're just a reoccurring nuisance.
Many enemies are now hidden around corners, impossible to predict, catching you with cheap attacks.
Imagine the clearing in Forest of the Giants, where you see the first Heide Knight sitting by the tree in the middle. Imagine your first playthrough, running around, alerting the 5 or 6 enemies laying down, and how much difficulty you probably had.
Now, imagine that instead of 5 or 6 enemies, it was over 15. With the same health/damage/behaviors as the 5 or 6.
Or, if your imagination isn't that good, take a look for yourself:
For a starting area, this is just plain stupid. I can't imagine new players will have much luck with this at all.
Some areas have new, much-needed shortcuts added, but not many that I've found so far.
Graphically, it looks pretty good - a little better than the original DS2, but with better lighting (in most places).

Just Cause 2, when it just came out, was a guilty pleasure. After so much time, there's guilt no more, just pleasure. And explosions.
If you are not familiar with the series, it follows adventures of Rico Rodriguez, hispanic secret agent serving Uncle Sam and usually taking down some dictatorship in tropical region. Just another Tuesday for a man who's will bends gravity, whose deeds can be seem from space and who's superstructure is impervious to high velocity air resistance.
You venture over humongous area of Panau, over 1000 square kilometeres of mountains, beaches, forests, roads, villages, military bases, sprinkled all around you. It's not a quality topping, as you can feel the brush of copy&paste here and there, but game's tempo and graphics that have charm straight off tropical postcards certainly make good job of covering it up, at least when you are not looking up close.
Spread mayhem accross ranks of corrupt military using your superb agility, agency special equipment, vehicles, guns, or surroundings using your grappling hook, that opens up movement as well as power to link objects, including fleshy ones, together for hilarious results. Panau space program consists of a high-pressure container, linked to nearby military personnel, followed by a gunshot to said container.
Whatever faults game had, be it story, voice acting, inability to work on Windows XP, they are thing of the past ,as for price Just Cause 2 is usually listed (75% off discounts and such) you can't deny game offers in terms of gameplay. For a price of a medium sandwich you get cheesy story, bad voice acting to laugh at and a killer game to enjoy.
Just cause it's a bit old, a bit dumb and a whole lot of cheap, doesn't mean Just Cause 2 can't blow you away. I strongly suggest you let it do so.

This is a hard game to recommend, but I do, because I enjoyed it. Not everyone will, though, and it's pretty safe to say that if you've heard any of the hype, you may enjoy this AND be disappointed all at once.
Gone Home is kind of in its own genre. It's not really a point and click adventure, because you're contained in one home for the entirity of the game. If I had to call it something, I'd call it a point-and-click virtual novella. The game can be finished before you hit the 3 hour mark, which makes it grossly overpriced. I expected the short length and bought it at about a 75% discount, and still feel like I overpaid a bit. I was expecting a shorter game that made up for its short length in story telling, which I was okay with paying for...but the story did leave a lot to be desired.
I won't repeat the game's original premise, because if you're interested enough in the game to read its reviews, you already know. If you go into this game knowing what to expect, you may enjoy it. This is not a horror game (for some reason, many people are under the impression it has scares), and this isn't a game that has much replayability. (And even then, the replayability is determined mostly by missable items and Easter eggs.) The story is quite cliched (with one small exception that I won't spoil here), though heartwarming at times and sad at others. The one thing this game does right is its subtle touches, things you may notice (or miss) that add to the story or give you details that change your perspective of what's going on. Though the story is not particularly special or memorable, it is genuinely intriguing to sift through the letters and belongings of this family, learning about their successes, failures, and disturbing secrets.
I was looking forward to this game ever since reading about it in an issue of GameInformer some time ago, and I think the amount of hype really led me to disappointment. Yes, the game was enjoyable, but it was certainly no Game of the Year. I can appreciate that the developers put time and effort into what was a great idea, and I love that this is a game that tells a story without ever needing to equip a weapon.
All in all, I would give this game a 6/10. This is an average quality game. Its downfalls include its lackluster story and its length, while its positives would be the atmosphere, sense of intrigue, and its subtly. Keep in mind before you buy that this is a very short game that you will probably only play once before never touching it again. If you are still interested, wait for a sale so that the price matches the quality and quantity of content.

This game is one of the best experiences I've had with PC gaming, or even gaming in general. A fantastically told story, deeply emotional, not to mention the detail with the hand-written notes, and custom-made game cartridge art for the game is just brilliant.
It might not be for everyone, since there is no combat, it's simply a game of exploration within a home, but I think that's perfectly fine. This isn't a game about combat or conflict, it's about discovery.
It is short, too, but I think that's good too. It means that the narrative that you discover and experience isn't dragged on unnecessarily. Some might complete it faster than others, but I found that I didn't want to. I wanted to just look in every nook and cranny, and piece together the lives of the people that lived inside the home, to pick up on the elements of their lives that they kept hidden from each other.
I can't guarantee you'll like it, but I think everyone should at least play through it, just to experience something like it.

I don't usually take reviews seriously, but the hate born because of From's marketing practices is just too much and people are actually giving this game bad scores based upon their disappointment with the company.
I'll try to be as objective as possible with this review. Do I agree with such practices? No, I do not. Do I think this should have been free? That's a bit questionable. Why? After seeing the things done with the game, I do think that this needed some effort to be done and effort costs money, the question is, is this tolerable knowing they promised us a game that was going to be supported? Kind of, knowing that it probably took some time to make and I'll say it again, time is money.
I do think that it should have been even cheaper, probably 10 Euros (I'm from Europe) or so would have been a fair price.
Lets look at the facts, this really is a paid "update" more or less, it does include some major changes to the game such as item placement and enemy placement which really do make a big difference compared to the initial experience and some graphical and performance upgrades.
Is it worth paying 15 Euros if you already beat the game or own the game, in my opinion yes, it does look better and does run better, the item and enemy repositioning makes the game feel fresh and an overall better experience. Don't forget that this probably wouldn't have even existed if it wasn't paid, because the people in From Soft need to eat as well. I hope that this review won't spawn hate, but objective and rational opinions based on what you read.
In short, I do not like the way they did it, but I do realize it probably wouldn't have been done for free. Is it worth it, I would say yes. Please stop giving this bad reviews because of how♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥you are, they did a good job with this "Special Edition" and it costs as much as a DLC pack would cost for any other game. I do see why people might be or are♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥of at From's marketing, but try understanding that we might have not even gotten this updated version if we didn't pay for it. People spend like 5-10 Euros for a dlc pack that contains a few weapons and a few virtual hats or masks and yet there is no one complaining about that and you people complain for paying 15 Euros for a remastered version of a game that launched one year ago.
Thank you for reading, I hope you re-consider about buying this.

Well dispite what everyone seemed to say ("don't buy this , They are moneygrabbers")
I decided to give it a try.
I already had DS2+DLCs.
So I wondered wether it would be worth the 15€ or not.
To all people with the same worry , fear not , It's worth the money. DEFINITLY!
First things first, I started game, nothing new so far, created a new game.
Nice lightning, my character also looks awesome!
Took the 3 items on the way to the firewitches, all good, nothing new gameplay-wise.
Created char, killed the first ogre for stonering and proceeded to do the tutorial.
Then the changes kept popping up, Stonestatue in the way, can't kill the other ogres, meh :/ , seems there are now basilisks in that area too.
Up to majula, grab the binos and up to Wood of fallen giants.
And then after grabbing a few items suddenly.
WTF AN OGRE IN THE BLOODY RIVER!
Well, ok free 1k souls, I thought, but this one does respawn, so make that 1k a splendid 10k and proceed towards the Heideknight.
O.K. There is no Heideknight . _ . No ZapZapSword, Instead houndreds of undead corpses, some just acting dead, so kill everyone, proceed.
And so on I was pleasantly suprised by the changes, Here a few monster more, there a different monster instead of another, the game felt "new".
Since i always wished i could play throu my favorite games anew this was perfect. I realy can experience it anew :)
Also many changes are suprising, since they increase the difficultylevel of the areas.
But the areas that get a hight boost in difficulty are usualy not areas a person new to Dark Souls would travel to early on. (Try to grab that flamesword from the lizzard now , be suprised by turtles )
So many many changes, none to the bosses so far, with the exeption beeing the alternativ Pursuer fight (location ).
Now all you hardcore fighters can happily face him with a few added undead enemys.
This is also a non-critical fight for fresh players, making the game harder for veterans and hard for freshies, a perfect change i think.
I couldn't even list all changes in that one simples zone but believe me, changes are plenty.
Also some changes are very lore-friendly, for instance undead trying to fell the giant-trees .
Oh and did i mention veterans can experience new harder fights?
Take a look at the new shiny dragon protecting the Blues in HeideTower of Flame, or the numerous neutral Heideknigts there (which can be aggroed ).
Or proceed to the lost bastille, PURSUERS .
PURSUERS EVERYWHERE !
And the PVP/COOP ?
Fantastic, always wanted to go 4v1 against a nooby host ?
I had this once in No-Man-Wharf, It was so epic !
You have to utilize every advantage and mob you can get .
Also go and kill these damm bellkeepers ffs.
All you katanafreaks be happy, You can get the sweet sweet flame after the pursuer boss fight.
So get it and buy ur Uchigatana.
Less awekward fights and more hardships that are fair. It has a good flow and better feel to it, me like!
Oh and the enviromental changes are a bliss, like No-Man-Wharf for example.
It's very dark, so get a torch, or alternativly, you can get the help of an undead torchholder (like in the undead crypts ) that follows you.
Making the area very hard for mages due to the missing lock on.
Add new enemys and you can be sure to have a tough time there.

So, I'm seeing a absolute buttload of negative reviews for this right now, and mainly for the sole reason of, "This is merely a cashgrab, you shouldn't buy this because From Software are ***holes, omg the graphics aren't even all that different." As of me writing this review, the front page has nothing but bad reviews, and the original's front page is mostly bad, with little good. Well, let's put this in perspective for the people who aren't absolutely stuck-up, over-emotional fools, shall we?
For new players:
This is now the cheapest iteration of the game, and provides a lot more challenge and content than the previous iteration. The new layout of enemies comes with easier and harder forms, as well as much more lore-based placement, such as certain knights in the right zone, recurring enemies that should no doubt populate the world a lot more than they did in the original, and twists not before seen.
It comes with all the DLCs wrapped up inside it as well, meaning no need for a season pass or seperate DLC buys. I'm told it even comes with an alternate ending, though I'm uncertain how this is attained.
Graphics only appear 'marginally' better, and I believe this is because our original community are so used to using mods to make it look better, that they can't understand this is a step up from the original. Plus I also don't believe people have the eyesight capable of differentiating between 2K and 4K textures, unless they're already ripping them and zooming in by 200% to compare pixels, which I doubt. You'll also see a lot of complaints about 'lighting being broken', and again, this is because of mods that changed the game's lighting and depth of field, and such things.
The core gameplay however is uncompromised. It plays exactly like DkS2 did, enemies act more or less the same, though I have noticed they have more aggro range and give up on you a lot harder than they used to, which disallows you to use their 'give up' boundary to cheese fights so easily, allowing for greater challenge. For those of you who've heard of the challenge of a Souls game, this embodies it a lot more than the original ever could.
Now I won't lie, I don't have as many hours on the original as most die hard players do. However, I'm a souls fan. I've played DeS into the dirt, and have over 1000 hours on DkS1 between 360 and PC editions. Though perhaps I cannot pretend to speak as loudly as the 'die hards', I too have a voice, therefore;
Old players of the Original:
Why do you insist on splitting our community so because of, as you call it, a 'cashgrab'? You're killing our community. You'te downvoting both games, turning old and new players away from it. Do you truly wish to see DkS2 die simply because you refuse to payout for a HD edition or because you prefer the original? This isn't a moment to be spiteful and bitter. We all love DkS2, do we not? This edition will no doubt draw a large crowd, and the original will lose its popularity in the face of it. I could say you ought to quit if you despise it that much, however I won't, as I'm not so black and white a person, but please stop attacking our community over it. Yes, From Software aren't the best company in the world. But at least it's not EA or Ubisoft, am I right?
Otherwise, I truly believe you might find enjoyment in the way this game has changed. For those of you with hundreds or thousands of hours, are you not just a little bored of knowing where every item and enemy is? Perhaps you feel as though DkS2 was not released as it should be?
This remake answers for a lot of flaws the original had, and you're willingly denying yourselves the chance to see an improved version. Again, perhaps not as improved as everyone would like, but it is an improvement. I, who pre-ordered the original DkS2, am thoroughly enjoying this game despite only having played it 9 hours (upon making this review).
However, I'm not demanding you spend your money on this game. Merely trying to make people understand this isn't as bad as a lot of people are making this out to be. Do you really want to kill DkS2 over a remake? Especially if the original is better? I don't think you do. I think you want Dark Souls to live for a long time, like a poor soul afflicted with the Hollow Curse.
And admittedly, there are bugs. I've seen some people can't open the game, some people can't make controllers work, or it crashes on specific screens or actions. The same is true of any game. All our computer rigs are different though. They all handle things differently. This isn't a console game where it's actually a problem that affects everyone. And remember, upon writing this review, the game's been out just over a full day. Do you guys remember when it'd take a week for an AAA release to get a patch to make it work after release?
I reccomend this game to new players who wish to see the unadulterated beauty that is DkS2, and old who're interested in reliving the feeling of uncertainty and peril of our first playthrough into Drangleic. DkS2:SofTS, as much as a lot of our community will hate to admit it, is the future of our beloved game. Buy it on sale, buy it full price, don't buy it at all. I'm not personally bothered. But don't read over the negative reviews filling the front page and presume this is a terrible game to buy. It's a great game. Better than a lot of the things we see nowadays.
I've said my piece, we'll see what people think of it, but know I won't be commenting or paying attention to the responses this review gets. I don't care to argue with anyone. All I know is, I love Dark Souls. If you do too, I hope to find you as enemy or friend in Drangleic.

Alright, 10 hours in.
Firstly, people have been saying that the Graphical upgrade is barely noticable. By and large, they are correct - the game still looks like DS2. Models are slightly crisper, a few improved textures here and there, but NOT worth the £20.00 upgrade for the Graphics upgrade alone. The main improvement is in the Lighting department - especially under Torchlight conditions, for example in the Gutter, wherein the light is smoother, shadows are better, the whole thing stutters a lot less - it's fairly awesome in comparison.
Gameplay wise, it's DS2 with all the DLCs and some expanded Flavour texts. However, the developers have also shifted enemy placements, added a few new enemies and many many more NPC Phantoms, Shades and Invaders. Combine this with the new maximum of 6 players (intended for 3v3) and many 'fun' multiplayer events can happen (From Software, whichever developer decided to add the Valley Children invaders in the Black Gulch, there is a spot in hell reserved just for you. I've seen 2 players + 2 AI wiped by 2 of those guys).
However, it all comes down to the simple fact that I was going to buy the DLCs anyway, and this version saved me a couple of Pounds and gave me a couple of boosts to boot! Excellent Value for someone in my position.
TL;DR
-I own DS2, but none of the DLCs
--Worth it if you enjoyed DS2 and/or want to play all the DLCs.
-I own DS2 and some/all of the DLCs
--Probably/Definitely not worth the cost, unless you're really into the Multiplayer and want some 3v3 action.
-I do not own DS2
--You should do. Buy this, it's excellent value for the full content.
All in all, gotten me back into DS again.

I purchased this during the Steam Summer Sale, and it's been a blast (from the past). Good gun play, great level design, authentic feel to everything. If you were ever like me and trying to stretch your dollar, you probably picked up a mod called WWI source. Verdun feels like that mod updated and made better.
However, there are a few problems with it:
Voice chat is restricted to your four man squad, and with up to 16 people on a team and 32 people playing across a map, sometimes the need to communicate important information in a time effective matter just doesnt cut it when typing things out.
You do have to lead your shots a little, if you ever played Battlefield, ARMA, Red Orchestra or Rising Storm, you'll be fine.
The game is also poorly optimized. Are you running a research program like Folding At Home or maybe a dimming program like
If you are, get ready to experince a sever frame rate drop and a crazy amount of lag on your end. The same applies at very high settings. Running at Ultra quality with all of the visual options (Minus v-sync and Windowed) on results in a give or take 60FPS depedning on the map, but at times, this can drop down to 20 for no real reason.
Lastly the community on this game is great, but since the summer sale, the more I return, the less players I find playing it. When It was first purchased there were clusters of full servers, and it seemed alive and well, and what I thought to be a good purchase. But now I'm finding half and quarter filled servers. even during peak hours on Friday nights, and on saturdays and sundays.
Bottom Line: It's a solid game with a lot of feel, but the emptying servers and the optimization issues hurt what is probably one of the best historical games I've played, and one of only a few that I've seen tackle the subject mater.

The graphics update is imperceptible some of the time, but overall the game seems to run more smoothly and some of the lighting and special effects are great! The only criticism I can find is that save games don't transfer over, so only upgrade if you feel like starting fresh! If you already own DS2 and the DLC, I wouldn't recommend buying, though, as you won't be getting your moneys worth without the benefit of getting the new content.

Few games have the power to elicit actual human emotions. Say what you will about the vast majority of many of the "great" narrative-driven games of the last 15 years, but 90% of them boil down to conventional player power-fantasies even if they're well written power-fantasies. Gone Home is so much more. Gone Home is one of the few games to truly harness the idea of a player interacting with a constructed virtual environment to craft a story built with human details and honest understanding. The game may lack combat or puzzles or other traditional modes of player progression/achievement, but it makes up for it in an all-encompassing and enveloping tale of love, coming of age, and family, and I can't name a single other game that comes half as close as Gone Home to telling a mature tale with such ease and depth of character. It was my Game of the Year for 2013 and easily one of my favorite games of the 2010s. It is a must play for anyone interested in games with true artistic ambition.

If you've never played this game or like me never purchased Dark Souls 2 on PC then I really recommend the DX11 version. The new Textures, the Lighting and the fixed Enemy placement makes this game worth the $49.99 I spent on it. Not to mention the silky smooth 60fps I am getting.

Overall this package ain't quite bad, If you wanted to play Dark Souls 2 the way it was meant to be played and the way it was advertised way back when I'd say get this version of the game. BUT if you wanted to play with Mods and don't want to wait, then I'd say get the DX9 version or if you already have the game, probably stick with that version, UNLESS you really want to experience the new changes and join the new community.

Gone Home Review
By now you have probably already heard of this game, why it is and isn't liked among certain crowds. I absolutely loved this game.
Gone Home is a game we don't see very often these days, one that focuses almost entirely on the storyline in substitution for gameplay. The Story and Voice Acting in this game are superb. The story compelled me to continue whenever I felt like stopping.
The Gameplay is going to be a disappointment if that is what you are looking for. If you are looking for a game with better gameplay, but not as interesting of a story then I would suggest the Novelist. The Gameplay isn't good, but it isn't bad. It'[s just [i]there[/i]. Nothing special was needed to make the story interesting, so that's what the creators gave. It doesn't intrude on how you experience the story, the story being progressed almost entirely through curiousity and deductiveness.
All in all, Gone Home is a great game, for certain people. If you are the kind of person who likes games with interesting gameplay taht don't need too much of a story, there are plenty of games like that on steam (some of which are free), but this game is not of that genre. If you are curious as to whether or not Gone Home is your type of game, I encourage you to try it out, I doubt you'll regret it.
For people that love stories, whether it be through books, movies, TV shows, etc, this game is made for you. The best way I can describe this game is as an interactive movie told from the first person.
The Gameplay is not really an issue once the story gets interesting, which may take a while for some people, this game can take some patience in the beginning. Is it replayable? Yeah, it is. I have played through this game twice, and on the second go I noticed things I had never noticed before, enhancing the story as a whole. The price is absolutely fair for what you get, even if the game isn't very long, the story itself is worth it.

I've played this on console and on PC. Before the "OMG I HATE YOU FROM AND BANDAI" trolls downvote my recommendation. I was incredibly iffy on spending the money on this since it's just Dark Souls II MK 2 but for the $20 price I got it for, I don't see anything wrong with buying it. Maybe it's wrong and maybe the features should of been there since launch but that doesn't matter. I'd still support a company I like so they can continue to make games. Now for the actual review
---------
It actually feels a lot better than it did in the base game. The frames feel better in some heavy traffic areas than they did before. Overall it feels like a polished game than a buggy unsupported game.
The enemy AI has actually improved a lot more than I had expected. I remember being able to cheese the enemies in the Forest without them backstepping me. Now they actually backstep and put up a fight. It also feels like the enemies will try to out-strategize you in some fights. With the Turtlemasters and the archers/firebomb throwers. Gives the game a nice crisp new feel to it.
Enemy placement got me quite easily. Wasn't ready for the Turtlemaster on the bridge near the ladder to the Pursuer's first encounter. Nor was I expecting the archer to shoot down arrows at me on my way to the Cardinal bonfire. I haven't gotten far into the game [Early lost bastille and up to the Dragonride boss fight] but the fights are nice. Especially with Heide's Knights actually being in the Tower of Flame, it actually makes sense now instead of them being spread out drastically across the game.
I normally never had a problem with my connection to the host but it feels a lot smoother than it did before, I have yet to PvP as well so hopefully there will be less lag-connected hits(even though that was a slight problem on my end and didn't seem like a major problem at all.)
I'm not sure if anyone else took this into account or even bothered to notice it like I did but the movesets and animations feel a lot smoother as well. Especially when low on STAM. Your punching hardly even stuns the enemy now and makes for a nice improvement, there is also the weapon movesets which I've noticed. It feels fluid(?) Using the broken straight sword and dagger on my Deprived felt weird. Felt like the Broken S.S was lagging behind a little to give that moveset it's "Heavy and slow" combo chains.
Would I recommend this game to new buyers? Yes, if you currently own the base game with all DLC or even if you don't own it, it's a nice change to the current game. Ignore all the salty kids that are upset about this apparent 'cash grab'.
For the price you can get it for depending on how much you actually own, you save quite a bit of money on the game.

A highly enjoyable sandbox game. See that image the game uses as it's logo? That could be you, on the back of a jet while another jet and his helicopter buddy is trying to gun you down.
The game runs well on a modern gameing rig, looks incredible and has such a vast playing area, that even I feel I have not finished exploring it yet. It does have a bare bones story attached to it, and some are put off by it, but rememeber, that isn't a sandbox games biggest highlight. Its biggest highlight is to be able to do anything you want, anywhere you want.
Go through the missions, cause mayhem and destruction. When you get tired of it, go hunting for collectables or just explore, by plane, car, helicopter or boat. There is a "extraction service", which is basically a teleportation service in the similar vein to quick traveling, but instead of just appearing where you want, you skydive out of a helicopter above where you want, for that dynamic entrance you always want.
Weapons vary from pistols, shotguns, sub machineguns, assault rifles and sniper rifles. Theres rockets, grnade launchers, grenades and TNT aswell. There are also agency vehicles, which can be upgraded to be more effective. The guns too can be upgraded. Buy the DLC and you get more agency vehicles and more guns. While not essential, still fun if you have the spare change for it all.
The map itself is large, with easter eggs dotted around for you to find. From tropical jungles and beaches, to deserts and snowy mountains, all populated with towns, military bases, airports, and cities, all connected by thousands of miles of road network.
Should you buy it? Ofcourse. Especially when its going for a fiver in the latest sales.
Should you buy the DLC? Only if you've put more than 24 hours into it. Then its safe to say you enjoyed the game enough that some extra guns and vehicles will enrich it somewhat.
PS: Theres a multiplayer mod now, there aren't any npcs in it, but 500 players all going nuts on the same server is a good trade off. Get some mates and group together for some fun. Plenty of servers aswell. Give it a go!

When I say "modified enemy placements", I mean adding an ogre to the first area you go to from Majula and replacing the first Heide knight with like 1000000 regular mobs. It's not the most exciting thing ever, but it certainly makes you think twice before parading into an area you thought you knew well.
Questionably worth the upgrade, but keep in mind it's basically the same price as all the DLC, so I'd say it's worth it if you were looking to pick up the DLC anyway.

A highly enjoyable sandbox game. See that image the game uses as it's logo? That could be you, on the back of a jet while another jet and his helicopter buddy is trying to gun you down.
The game runs well on a modern gameing rig, looks incredible and has such a vast playing area, that even I feel I have not finished exploring it yet. It does have a bare bones story attached to it, and some are put off by it, but rememeber, that isn't a sandbox games biggest highlight. Its biggest highlight is to be able to do anything you want, anywhere you want.
Go through the missions, cause mayhem and destruction. When you get tired of it, go hunting for collectables or just explore, by plane, car, helicopter or boat. There is a "extraction service", which is basically a teleportation service in the similar vein to quick traveling, but instead of just appearing where you want, you skydive out of a helicopter above where you want, for that dynamic entrance you always want.
Weapons vary from pistols, shotguns, sub machineguns, assault rifles and sniper rifles. Theres rockets, grnade launchers, grenades and TNT aswell. There are also agency vehicles, which can be upgraded to be more effective. The guns too can be upgraded. Buy the DLC and you get more agency vehicles and more guns. While not essential, still fun if you have the spare change for it all.
The map itself is large, with easter eggs dotted around for you to find. From tropical jungles and beaches, to deserts and snowy mountains, all populated with towns, military bases, airports, and cities, all connected by thousands of miles of road network.
Should you buy it? Ofcourse. Especially when its going for a fiver in the latest sales.
Should you buy the DLC? Only if you've put more than 24 hours into it. Then its safe to say you enjoyed the game enough that some extra guns and vehicles will enrich it somewhat.
PS: Theres a multiplayer mod now, there aren't any npcs in it, but 500 players all going nuts on the same server is a good trade off. Get some mates and group together for some fun. Plenty of servers aswell. Give it a go!

This is an FPS game that needed to be made for a long time. With so many WWII, futuristic, and various other FPS, squad based games out there, WWI tended to be overlooked as a premise for this kind of game. No longer...
This game is about as historically on-point, gritty, realistic, and tough as nails as it gets for a FPS. Here are some pros and cons:
CONS
- One hit kills, which means you will die A LOT. So, very little room for error
- Prone blocking, which means you will sometimes be under heavy fire and you can't lay flat on some surfaces and subsequently, will get gunned down cause you couldn't get low enough
- Can become frustrating at times because the rest of your squad doesn't work together or communicate, hence making it all that harder to win a match
- Current version does not currently feature other powers who were involved in the Great War. Russia and the Austro-Hungarian Empire come to mind.
PROS
- Lets you slip into a time warp and you really feel like you are there with the music, environment, weaponry, chemical warfare, and trench fighting that make up the game
- Challenging (as I said, one hit kills). Plus, you need to be strategic to survive. No run-and-gun gameplay here. That will only get you killed. The game will force you to utilize cover, work together as a squad, and test your ability to hold a location when defending and to force an enemy out of their trench after charging thru the deadly no-man's land
- Relatively good price and a great time waster for the money
- Developers are active, responsive, and want to hear your input
- Easy controls to learn
- Many different historically accurate unit types to master and level up
That's just brushing the surface. Point is, if you like FPS squad games, this will test your mettle and make COD or similar titles feel very childish and simple by comparison. Definitely worth your time!

Is this game fun with friends? Yes.
Playing mostly PVE playlists the game can be extremely fun when with a group of players that know their role and work well in a group setting. Missions and tower raids are reminiscent of mmo raids somewhat, except with a FPS vibe.
The A.I. can be lackluster at times, but the mechanics of the game are sound. A band-aid dispenser, a bullet hose, a welder, and a snipper all have useful roles. Customization is is nice as well, with all gear, guns, and outfits being available with the in-game currency. While shooting can be shoddy due to lag, guns are satisfying. From personal playtime most guns are fun and viable to use. In a PVE setting the best of the best of the killing machines is never required. The UI is simple and easy to navigate.
The developers have been very active with the game such as daily map rotations, promos for free gear. and updates/hotfixes. Guns and gear also have a cycle as well. In fact, many recent changes have been for the better, with the shop changing to in game currency reducing the pay-to-win structure that turned off many players in the past.
Sadly though the community and its mentality of its players makes this game a total turn-off. Playing with randoms is damn-near impossible; players vote-kick without reason, people loving to micromanage and ♥♥♥♥♥ about everything other players do, and while hacking is seen once and while due to no real anticheat system, players accuse others non-stop of being a hacker/cheater more than the actual act itself. The paranoia and ego of players in this game is sickening. I can see competition in PVP happening, but when everyone is going towards a common goal in PVE, who really cares if someone can get more kills than you? ITS PVE.
I love the mechaincs of the game and focused effort to make teamwork prosper, but the community makes it fall flat. If you want to deal with squeakers calling haxxxx and people thinking its time for xxXX420nosc0peblazeitXXxx this is the game for you. Otherwise, into the trash it goes.
